description: Works out a glaze slurry's specific gravity (SG) from the grams 100 mL of it weighs (or takes the SG), then, for a bucket of it and a target SG, the water to add, or to pour off after the glaze settles, as the recipe page's Specific gravity and water does. The water to add needs nothing else. The dry glaze per litre and the dry glaze and water the bucket holds (Brongniart's formula) need the dry materials' own SG: give drySg, or give the recipe's lines and it is estimated from each material (its mineral's measured density; 2.6 for commercial feldspars and clays; a frit from its oxides by Appen's glass factors), with drySgBasis saying how. Materials with no estimate (bentonite, stains, mixed borates, a potter's own) may be up to 5% of the weight and are left out; with more, there is no estimate. A drySg given wins over the estimate. Nothing is assumed otherwise. Water is 1; many dipping glazes are mixed near 1.4 to 1.5, but the right SG is the one that gives the thickness you tested.

drySg.description: The dry materials' own SG, if known. Only the dry weights need it. Wins over an estimate.

gramsPer100ml.description: What 100 mL of the slurry weighs, in grams.

lines.description: The recipe's materials, to estimate the dry materials' SG when drySg is not given.

amount.description: Its amount in the recipe, in any unit the other lines share (grams, parts, percent).

analysis.description: Only for a material not in the library: its oxides in weight percent, as { "SiO2": 68.5, "Al2O3": 17.4 }.

loi.description: Its loss on ignition in percent, with an analysis.

material.description: The material, by its name in the Glazecalc library ("Custer Spar", "Whiting", "EPK"), or your own name when you give its analysis.

litres.description: How much slurry is in the bucket, in litres.

sg.description: The SG, if already measured. Give this or gramsPer100ml.
